searchText: <drinkcoffee2022> I am about to kick off a draft EIP / RIP for blockchain client <> prover API. I recall talk of the EIP process being split out. Has this new process come into affect? Is there any documentation on the new process? <SamWilsn> If it's an ERC, it goes in `ethereum/ERCs`, otherwise it stays in `ethereum/EIPs` <drinkcoffee2022> where the API ^^^ would help facilitate decentralized sequencers; allow any prover to connect to any blockchain client. <e_nyc> Yeah this split went live as of yesterday, October 25 (re @drinkcoffee2022: I am about to kick off a draft EIP / RIP for blockchain client <> prover API. I recall talk of the EIP process being split out. Has this new process come into affect? Is there any documentation on the new process?) <e_nyc> From the looks of it, your proposal might be an ERC <drinkcoffee2022> OK thanks <drinkcoffee2022> I think the doc will come down to defining a JSON RPC API. <drinkcoffee2022> However, I think this API has implications on proof of consensus and briding, as that information is part of the information the blockchain client returns to the prover. <SamWilsn> Is it something you expect Ethereum clients to implement? (re @drinkcoffee2022: I think the doc will come down to defining a JSON RPC API.) <SamWilsn> If so, https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis might be the better location to define it. There's a lot of ambiguity around where these kinds of things get specified right now :/ <drinkcoffee2022> >Is it something >you expect Ethereum >clients to implement? They could choose to. It would allow them to be used as part of a decentralized sequencer. Initially, we (Immutable) would plan to put it into our fork of Geth. <drinkcoffee2022> I think I will start as an eip format as, on reflection there is a range of information, the RPC is just part of it (re @SamWilsn: If so, https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis might be the better location to define it. There's a lot of ambiguity around where these kinds of things get specified right now :/)

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <drinkcoffee2022> I am about to kick off a draft EIP / RIP for blockchain client <> prover API. I recall talk of the EIP process being split out. Has this new process come into affect? Is there any documentation on the new process?

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <SamWilsn> If it's an ERC, it goes in `ethereum/ERCs`, otherwise it stays in `ethereum/EIPs`

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <drinkcoffee2022> where the API ^^^ would help facilitate decentralized sequencers; allow any prover to connect to any blockchain client.

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <e_nyc> Yeah this split went live as of yesterday, October 25 (re @drinkcoffee2022: I am about to kick off a draft EIP / RIP for blockchain client <> prover API. I recall talk of the EIP process being split out. Has this new process come into affect? Is there any documentation on the new process?)

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <e_nyc> From the looks of it, your proposal might be an ERC

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <drinkcoffee2022> I think the doc will come down to defining a JSON RPC API.

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <drinkcoffee2022> However, I think this API has implications on proof of consensus and briding, as that information is part of the information the blockchain client returns to the prover.

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content: <SamWilsn> Is it something you expect Ethereum clients to implement? (re @drinkcoffee2022: I think the doc will come down to defining a JSON RPC API.)

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<SamWilsn> If so, https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis might be the better location to define it.

There's a lot of ambiguity around where these kinds of things get specified right now :/

excerpts.author: bridge-bot
excerpts.content:
<drinkcoffee2022> >Is it something 
>you expect Ethereum 
>clients to implement?
They could choose to. It would allow them to be used as part of a decentralized sequencer. Initially, we (Immutable) would plan to put it into our fork of Geth.
